description: A monophonic step sequencer programmed on a piano roll grid, holding 64 patterns of up to 16 measures, with pitch, gate, retrigger and velocity outputs and inputs for recording into the grid

inputs.text: Each rising edge advances the sequence by one division; pulses arriving while the module is paused are ignored, and there is no internal clock
Each trigger flips the sequence between running and paused, without reading whether the clock is actually running
A trigger sets the play position back to the start of the pattern, so that the next clock pulse plays the first note
Selects the pattern by pitch: 0V picks the first of the 64 and every semitone above that picks the next one
A trigger arms recording, which begins when the play position wraps round to the start of the pattern; a second trigger cancels the arming or stops the recording
The pitch written into the step being played while recording, quantised to the nearest semitone
A level above 1V while recording makes the step being played sound, and a level below 0.1V at the start of a step silences it
A level above 1V while recording marks the step being played to retrigger, and a level below 0.1V at the start of a step clears that mark
Sets the velocity written into the step being played while recording, 0-10V mapped onto the step's own 0 to 1 velocity

outputs.text: Carries the clock input unchanged, for chaining the clock on to another piano roll
Carries the run input unchanged, for chaining the run signal on to another piano roll
Carries the reset input unchanged, for chaining the reset on to another piano roll
The pattern now selected, as a pitch: 0V for the first and a twelfth of a volt for each one after, rather than the copy of the PTRN input the manual describes
Carries the record input unchanged, for chaining the record signal on to another piano roll
The pitch of the step now playing, 0V for C4 and a twelfth of a volt per semitone; while a gate above 1V is present at GATE the unquantised 1V/OCT input comes out here instead
10V while the step now playing sounds. With nothing patched to RTRG it drops to 0V for 1ms where a retrigger falls, and with nothing patched to RUN a gate lasts at most 2 seconds
A 1ms 10V pulse at the start of a step that follows a silent step, and at the start of any step marked to retrigger
The velocity of the step now playing, 0-10V
A 1ms 10V pulse when the last step of the pattern has been played

notes: left-clicking a cell in the grid makes that note sound, right-clicking an active note marks it to retrigger, and shift-dragging a note up or down sets its velocity
clicking the strip above the grid moves the play position and sounds the note there, and dragging across it plays along
clicking the strip below the grid picks the measure; holding on a measure for a second loops that measure alone, and holding again releases it
the readouts beside the grid are clicked with the left button, not the right, and each opens its own list
the pattern readout steps down or up when clicked at its ends, and opens a list of the 64 patterns when clicked in its middle
the readouts under the pattern number open lists headed Measures, Beats Per Measure and Divisions Per Beat, 1 to 16 of each
the bottom readout beside the grid shows whether the sequence is running, paused or recording, and clicking it starts or pauses it
the pattern readout ignores clicks while a cable is patched to PTRN, because the pattern is then chosen by that input
a new Piano Roll has an empty grid and plays nothing until notes are put into it by left-clicking cells, or recorded through the record inputs
the module has no clock of its own; nothing advances until a clock is patched to CLOCK
shift-dragging up or down on the module name changes the colour of the panel, and holding ctrl as well makes the change finer
menu: Copy Pattern — copies the pattern now selected; a Paste Pattern item then appears in the same menu and writes the copy over whatever pattern is selected when you click it
Copy Measure — copies the measure now selected; a Paste Measure item then appears in the same menu and writes the copy over whatever measure is selected when you click it
Clear Notes — empties every note in the pattern now selected
Notes to Show — a heading over the choices 12, 18, 24, 36, 48 and 60, setting how many rows of the grid are drawn
Clock Delay (samples) — a heading over the choices 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10, holding the clock input back by that many samples so a pattern change can arrive first
Driver Mode — makes a run or reset signal pick the first step at once rather than waiting for a clock pulse, so a piano roll driving another selects the pattern first
